sections.label: Core types
items: `int`, `float`: numbers. `str`: text. `bool`: True/False. `None`: explicitly no value.
`list`: ordered, mutable. `dict`: key/value pairs. Both are the shapes model responses and tool arguments come back as.

sections.label: String basics
items: `f"{x} tokens"`: f-strings, the standard way to build a string from variables.
`s.strip()`, ````s.startswith("```")````, `s.replace(",", "")`: the string methods this course's repair patterns lean on most.
`len(s)` works on strings, lists, and dicts alike: the length/count you'll compute constantly for budgets and validation.

sections.label: Lists and iteration
items: `for item in items:`: the loop shape behind chunking, retrieval scoring, and eval suites.
`[x for x in items if cond]`: a list comprehension, a filter written in one line, exactly the shape of a threshold filter.
Slicing: `items[:k]`: first k items, the mechanism behind top-k.

sections.label: Dictionaries
items: `d.get("key", default)`: read a key that might not exist, without raising, use this instead of `d["key"]` whenever a field might be missing.
`"key" in d`: checks presence only, an empty string still counts as present, presence isn't the same as usable.
`d["key"] = value`: set/overwrite a key.

sections.label: Functions and try/except
items: `def f(a, b=default):`: a function with a default argument.
`try: ... except Exception as e: ...`: catch a failure instead of letting it crash the whole program, the pattern behind every safe_call wrapper in this course.
Never use a bare `except:` with no type, it silently swallows even a genuine bug (like a typo) alongside the failure you meant to catch.

sections.label: JSON
items: `json.loads(text)`: text to a Python object (dict/list). Raises on malformed input.
`json.dumps(obj)`: a Python object back to a JSON string.
A raised `json.JSONDecodeError` from `loads()` is exactly the signal this course's repair pass exists to catch and fix before re-attempting.

sections.label: Async, in one paragraph
items: `async def f(): ...` defines a coroutine. `await f()` runs it and waits for the result, this is the shape every real model-API call takes (a network call you wait on), even though this course's Worker/Pyodide sandboxes run your exercise code synchronously for simplicity.

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Using `d["key"]` on a field that might be missing instead of `d.get("key")`, causing an uncaught `KeyError`.
A bare `except:` that hides real bugs along with expected failures.
Comparing floats with `==` when a small rounding difference is expected, use a tolerance instead.
